Applied.description:
What berth recorded on a host when it applied the configuration: its own
version, the plugins whose features the host has, and the provisioners
those features offer.

oneOf.description:
The host's device on the tailnet, as its Tailscale client saw it at
the end of the apply, when it is on one.

AppliedPlugin.description: A plugin as it was when a host's configuration was applied.

digest.description: SHA-256 of its files, so a change without a new version shows too.

choices.description: A command whose lines are the values to offer.

confirm.description:
For a yes or no: the question to answer yes to before the action
runs with it on, instead of the action's own.

fixed.description:
Why it keeps its default here and cannot be given another value,
such as destroying a machine no provisioner made. The screens show
it greyed and say this instead of changing it. Empty when it can be
changed.

help.description: What it is for, in a sentence or two, beside its short label.

kind.description:
`resource` for an argument of a provisioner that sizes the machine:
its CPUs, memory or disk. `text` for one whose value has several
lines. `boolean` for a yes or no, which the screens show as a switch.
Empty for any other argument.

secret.description:
What is given is a secret, such as a password: it is not shown as it
is typed, nor kept, nor written to a job's output.

values.description:
The values a provisioner's argument takes, when it is a choice of a
few. Empty for one that takes any text.

CommandLine.description: A list of arguments, or one string for `sh -c`.

agent_env.description: A wrapper that gives the agent its environment.

roots.description: Folders the file calls may touch.

simulated.description:
Whether the host is simulated: in single-user mode its commands then
run through `agent_env` too, and its version says so.

systemd.description:
Whether the calls that need systemd work. Off in single-user mode
unless set.

units.description: Units whose state the stats report.

From.description: Who did something, as berthd saw it.

HostAction.description:
An action of the host's controller: an entry of `/etc/berth/actions.json`.
Listed without `run`.

extends.description: Actions it is a step of; it then has no row of its own.

input.description: What the workstation sends on standard input: `secrets`.

HostType.description:
What berth does with a host: what its profile means it to be, or what it
was seen to be. They are in the order of how much of berth each has.

KeptProfile.description:
The profile a host keeps of itself, at `/etc/berth/profile.json`: the
profile as berth holds it, without the enrollment key and without its
`access`, how the berth that wrote it reaches the host. A berth that does
not have the host can take it over from this.

berth.description: The version of the berth that wrote it.

format.description:
The format of this document: 2, or 1 for one berth 0.4.1 wrote, whose
profile has the layout before `access`.

host.description: The name the host has in the berth that wrote it.

instance.description: The same in a document of format 1.

machine.description:
The record of the machine berth created for the host, as a resource,
when it did.

written.description: When it was written, in RFC 3339.

cursor.description: Give it back as `since` to go on from here.

next.description: Pass as `since` for the rest, when there is more.

Offer.description:
Provisioners a feature of a host offers, as its tasks found them: berth
registers each under a name of its own that names the host. The host
serves this to anyone who may read it, so it holds public values only,
such as a server's certificate, never a key.

aliases.description:
Other values of a setting that reach the same server, such as the
name a berth server on the host gives it: a provisioner registered by
hand with one of them is named to its owner, who can make it the
host's.

fingerprint.description:
What the host says identifies the server, such as the fingerprint of
its certificate, for the person who reads the report.

provisioners.description: The plugin's provisioners it offers, by their ids in the plugin.

secrets.description:
Values of the provisioners' secrets, such as the certificate of the
server to pin, kept as the provisioners' own.

settings.description:
Values of the provisioners' own arguments. `{address}`, `{user}` and
`{port}` stand for where berth reaches the host and as whom.

first_offset.description: Where what is still kept begins, when the start was dropped.

lines.description: The same as text, when read by lines.

offset.description: The offset this answer starts at.

cpu_time.description: Seconds of CPU used so far.

PublishFrame.description: What a client sends over the channel stream to publish.

action.description:
The action it was started for, if any. The sessions an older
berthd kept on the host say `task`.

lost.description: It ended with berthd or the host, not by itself.

input.description: Text for standard input; a process then sees the end of its input.

timeout.description: Seconds after which the command is ended.

Started.description:
The answer to a start with `wait=`: the session and, when it has ended in
time, what it wrote.

cpu.description: Percent busy over 200 ms, all cores together.

TailnetDevice.description:
A host's device on the tailnet, from `tailscale status --json`. It
holds public values only, which the control server's API finds it by.

dns_name.description: Its MagicDNS name, such as `studio.example.ts.net`, without the final dot.

host_name.description: The machine's own hostname, as the client reports it.

id.description:
The device's stable id: Tailscale's `nodeId`, or the number of
Headscale's node.

tailnet.description: The tailnet's name, when the client knows it.

oneOf.description:
What the host's configuration was last applied from, when berth
recorded it. An older berthd does not say.

simulated.description:
Whether it is simulated, as `berth serve --simulate` and its hosts
are: nothing it does reaches a real machine.

oneOf.description:
What was installed on the host, by that record: `managed` when
only the controller was, `workstation` for a whole profile. Absent
when the host keeps no record.
